stories.headline: LoC villages await bunkers despite shelling threat
stories.title: LoC villages await bunkers despite shelling threat
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 16: More than a year after Operation Sindoor, residents living along the Line of Control (LoC) in Uri sector of north Kashmir’s Baramulla district say they continue to live under the threat of cross-border shelling, with no new community bunkers visible on the ground. Residents said that despite repeated demands for safe shelters, the construction of new bunkers has not progressed in several border villages. They also claimed that many of the existing bunkers have either deteriorated or are no longer fit to provide adequate protection during shelling. Lal Hussain Kohli, a resident of Charunda village along the LoC, told Rising Kashmir that no new bunker has been constructed in the area since Operation Sindoor. “Not a single new bunker has been built by the government in the last one year. Whatever bunkers we have were constructed nearly five years ago,” he said. Kohli said the village remains vulnerable to cross-border firing and requires functional shelters for the protection of civilians. “There are around eight community bunkers here, but all of them are in a dilapidated condition and cannot be used safely,” he said. Similar concerns were raised by residents of other border villages, including Garkote, Mothal and Silikote. Bashir Ahmad Bhat of Garkote said villagers had received no government support for bunker construction after Operation Sindoor. “If cross-border shelling happens again, where are we supposed to go?” he asked, adding that some families had been forced to construct makeshift shelters using their own limited resources. “We are poor people, but we have no choice. We have to protect our families,” Bhat said. Nadeem Abbasi, an ex-sarpanch of Gawalta village along LoC said that no new bunker had been constructed in the village and residents continued to face serious risks during any escalation along the LoC. “No new bunker has come up here. Our lives continue to remain at risk,” Abbasi said, adding that several older bunkers had also deteriorated and could no longer safely accommodate residents during shelling. The issue of civilian shelters in Uri has remained a concern for years. In 2020, the government had proposed the construction of several community bunkers in the border area. While some were completed, residents said many remained unfinished or inadequate. In May last year, the then Deputy Commissioner, Baramulla, approved the construction of 202 overhead protection trenches in the Uri sector. However, some residents questioned their effectiveness and termed them a waste of public money. “They dug shallow trenches and covered them with wooden planks and mud. Such structures are unsafe during heavy shelling. We need proper concrete bunkers,” said Tariq Hashim, a resident of Kamalkote sector. The issue gained further attention in January this year when then Deputy Commissioner Baramulla Minga Sherpa said that the Home Department had sanctioned more than 500 bunkers to be constructed along the LoC in Uri. However, residents said there was little visible progress on the ground and urged the administration to expedite the construction of durable and fully equipped shelters before any fresh escalation along the LoC. When contacted, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Uri Prince Kumar said the matter had already been taken up with the higher authorities. “A proposal in this regard has already been sent to the government,” he told Rising Kashmir.

stories.headline: CS orders faster rollout of MHA-approved Rs 1579-Cr disaster package
stories.title: CS orders faster rollout of MHA-approved Rs 1579-Cr disaster package
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 16: Chief Secretary Atal Dulloo on Sunday reviewed the implementation of the Recovery and Reconstruction (R&R) Plan-2025 and utilisation of the disaster recovery assistance sanctioned for Jammu and Kashmir by the Centre directing departments to accelerate project formulation and execution while ensuring that every reconstructed asset is made more resilient to future disasters. The Chief Secretary took detailed stock of the Rs 1579.09 crore recovery package approved by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) under the NDRF and SDRF R&R Funding Window. The same was approved through MHA for Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) for damages caused by floods, cloudbursts, landslides and other disasters to the tune of Rs 1534.58 crore, besides Rs 44.52 crore for the dedicated Ramban District recovery plan following the April 2025 cloudburst and flash floods. Reviewing the progress, the Chief Secretary noted that departments have so far prepared costed action plans amounting to Rs 1225.78 crore, leaving a balance of Rs 353.31 crore to be operationalised by the Jal Shakti and Agriculture sectors. Emphasising that disaster recovery should not merely restore damaged infrastructure to its pre-disaster condition, the Chief Secretary directed all executing agencies to strictly follow the ‘Build Back Better’ (BBB) approach. Dulloo also called for strict cross-verification of beneficiary lists and project proposals with major ongoing schemes, including PMAY-G, JalJeevan Mission, AMRUT, SASCI, NABARD, PMGSY and Samagra Shiksha, to eliminate any possibility of duplication and ensure optimal use of public resources. He called for reconstructed assets to incorporate appropriate disaster-resilient features, including compliance with Seismic Zone IV/V requirements, elevated plinths and slope stabilization measures, wherever applicable. The departments were also asked to optimally utilise both norm-based and flexible assistance available under the approved recovery framework to meet incremental resilience requirements. The Chief Secretary further directed that all projects be geo-tagged forthwith and uploaded on the BEAMS digital platform, creating a unified digital record for monitoring progress, financial utilization and physical outcomes. Giving the sector-wise review, the Principal Secretary, DMRR&R, Chandraker Bharti revealed that significant progress has been achieved in several components of the recovery programme. In the social sector, he highlighted against an approved allocation of Rs 289.40 crore, departments have formulated plans amounting to Rs 262.11 crore. Similarly in the Housing component 100 percent commitment of its Rs 193.19 crore allocation, covering 9083 households, including 5227 fully and 3856 severely damaged houses has been achieved. With respect to the Roads and Bridges component, it has emerged as one of the strongest performing infrastructure segments, with its entire Rs 461.64 crore allocation planned for restoration of approximately 1230.7 km of roads and 4494.5 metres of bridges. Additionally, the power sector has planned utilisation of Rs 70.08 crore against Rs 72.97 crore, targeting restoration of more than 21,000 poles, 1100 circuit kilometres of conductors and 800 transformers, benefiting around 1.45 lakh consumers. The meeting was apprised that the drinking water and sanitation has so far formulated plans for Rs 59.02 crore against Rs 139.65 crore, while Irrigation and Flood Control has planned Rs 93.01 crore against Rs 199.79 crore and are in a process of utilising the full kitty of funds available. In the productive sectors, agriculture has formulated plans worth Rs 168.36 crore against Rs 223.67 crore, covering 45 packages relating to crop inputs, land reclamation and restoration of research infrastructure at SKUAST-Jammu. Animal husbandry and livestock has planned Rs 8.86 crore against Rs 10.28 crore, while horticulture has fully utilised its Rs 3.87 crore allocation to support 3493 farmers. The Chief Secretary also reviewed the dedicated Rs 44.52 croreRamban recovery plan prepared in response to the cloudburst and flash floods of April 19-20, 2025. The plan includes Rs 23.24 crore for roads and bridges, Rs 3.34 crore for irrigation and flood control, Rs 1.78 crore for education and Rs 1.48 crore for animal husbandry and livestock, with approved and proposed allocations fully reconciled in these components. The Chief Secretary directed that household relief under the recovery programme be disbursed strictly in accordance with the 30:40:30 progress-linked Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) pattern, ensuring that payments remain aligned with actual progress of reconstruction. He directed block, sub-divisional, and district-level nodal officers to ensure complete resolution of E-Samadhan and CPGRAMS grievances within 15 days, making grievance redressal an integral part of the recovery monitoring mechanism. The Chief Secretary underscored that the recovery programme should result not only in timely restoration of damaged assets but also in a more resilient and disaster-ready J&K, with every rupee sanctioned translating into durable public infrastructure and tangible relief for affected communities. The meeting was attended by Additional Chief Secretary, Finance; Additional Chief Secretary, PWD; Principal Secretary, DMRR&R; Director, CD and SDRF; Administrative Secretaries, Divisional Commissioner, Jammu/Kashmir; and other senior officers. Deputy Commissioners from all 20 districts participated virtually.
